parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs an operative parent layer — Supreme-Court-allowed passport/visa sex restrictions (X markers barred, discrepancy-driven refusal, possible fraud ineligibility), a federal ban on single-sex facilities, federal custody conversion-therapy and immigration-detention abuse, hostile national framing, and multiple foreign travel advisories — with a comparatively restrained state: no documented facility ban, gubernatorial vetoes of bathroom bills, municipal public-accommodation ordinances, national hate-crime coverage, and a July 2026 low-risk designation. State protections cannot cancel federal entry, facility, or custody exposure. No trans-directed violence is documented here, but the dossier warns silence is not safety; Pride collapse signals deterioration. Minors face documented state and national youth restrictions. Net: Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal regime limits markers to M/F per sex at birth, halted X-marker processing; visa cable directs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and invites fraud/lifetime-ineligibility consideration; travellers report blocked or confiscated documents; eight-plus foreign governments issued travel advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Litigation pending; fraud finding requires four elements with limited waivers and is never automatic; existing X-marker passports remain valid to expiry.
entry_documents.interaction: Border screening feeds into detention, where federal custody policies then apply; a mismatch can cascade from refusal to fraud allegation to custody.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: From 2026 federal corrections policy mandates conversion-therapy-style regime (hair cutting, hormone removal, substituted psychiatric drugs); immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans detainees. State retains gay/trans panic defence and its hate-crime statute omits gender identity.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute has covered gender identity since 2009; several executive orders are enjoined or challenged.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any state-level police encounter can escalate into federal custody governed by the hostile corrections policy.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Parent order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities nationwide. The state has no documented mapped ban, but the equality map notes other sex-definition laws may still affect access, and neighbouring jurisdictions criminalize use.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Governor vetoed bathroom and pronoun bills in June 2023; state placed in July 2026 low-risk group for targeting transgender adults.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local restraint does not displace the federal facility rule in federally funded buildings.

care_services.exposure: State bars sex-reassignment surgery on trans children; 1982 Medicaid surgery exclusion remains unresolved against later orders; state youth-targeting policies flagged; patient records subpoenaed nationally; hostile national posture toward minors' care.
care_services.protection: June 2023 order extends Medicaid/gender-affirming coverage to state employees over 21; birth-certificate and licence marker changes permitted.
care_services.interaction: A visiting minor's care needs intersect federal and state youth restrictions with no clear visitor carve-out.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy targets groups 'radically pro-transgender'; justice-department memo uses 'radical gender ideology'; executive orders use mutilation framing; 66% poll supports birth-sex document rules; Pride organising in the second-largest city collapsed in January 2026.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward is not keyed to trans ideology; strategy states it will not target mere disagreement; courts blocking orders; state designated low-risk for adults.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National threat framing raises exposure probability wherever state-level restraint is the only shield.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bans surgery on trans children, bars trans girls from female sports, runs an education reporting hotline; national order directs criminal investigation of teachers facilitating social transition; national youth-care hostility.
minors_guardians.protection: Assessment judges youth policies unlikely to extend to adults; parental recognition for same-sex parents upheld.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor carries both state youth measures and federal rhetoric into schools, clinics and any investigation.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-directed violence, arrest or detention specific to this state is documented; gay/trans panic defence remains available; national bias statistics track orientation more than identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; municipal ordinances protect in nine cities; well-documented dossier with no recorded pattern is mildly positive.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Dossier explicitly warns the absence of incidents is not evidence none occurred.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Protections are a patchwork of federal rulings, a gubernatorial order, a justice-department interpretation and exempt-laden municipal ordinances; Medicaid conflict unresolved; measures may lapse with administration change; litigation on documents and orders unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties union suit ongoing; legal-aid FAQ on document rules; courts have enjoined several orders; low-risk designation.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies reach services and employment but not federal entry screening, federal facilities or federal custody.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: an unremedied birth-sex facility rule plus polite everyday life. Ours is worse at entry — visa refusal and fraud exposure, X-marker ban, custody conversion-therapy policy — but narrower on facilities (federal buildings only, no documented state ban) and better locally through vetoes, municipal ordinances and a low-risk designation.

Lower than this: pervasive visitor-facing service denial at scale with dead-end complaints and majority threat-framing. Here mass service refusal is not documented in this state and protections demonstrably operate (veto, ordinances, courts). Only the parent document regime approaches that severity, and it is contested in litigation.

Ours rates lower: 0.65-B pairs local hostility with enforced readmissions, compensation and prosecutions, no universal federal restriction. Here the parent layer imposes universal document, facility and custody exposures with no effective remedy reaching them, which the state layer cannot displace.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one system: a restrictive, largely unremedied federal layer (document and visa regime, federal single-sex facility ban, hostile custody policies, national threat framing, foreign travel advisories) sitting on a state that has actively declined to add its own hostile layer — vetoes of bathroom bills, marker-change litigation won, municipal public-accommodation ordinances, national hate-crime coverage, and a July 2026 low-risk ranking for targeting adults. Those local protections shape everyday life but do not reach the border, federal buildings, or federal custody, so the parent's tier-1 exposures govern the rating's floor. Deteriorating climate signals (Pride collapse, youth-targeting policies, pending bills) and unresolved litigation pull downward; documented local restraint and functioning remedies pull upward, yielding Elevated Risk.
